elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it (Vendor assigns)
elements.evidence: "If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials." — the Type I definition/assignment paragraph (b) is not in the supplied text, and IBM still "will identify them as being 'Type I Materials,' 'Type II Materials'", so IBM may designate work product as IBM-owned Type II."; no express assignment language is added.,
"Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: Licence runs only to "copies of Type II Materials"; there is no licence to Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned (Type I) deliverables.

"no Materials or data will be jointly owned"

offending_extra_words: modify and prepare derivative works based on, and sublicense
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the preferred embedded-IP licence is absent: no licence is granted to Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned deliverables — the grant is confined to "copies of Type II Materials".

Customer ownership of deliverables rests solely on flipping the default to Type I; no assignment obligation is added and IBM retains discretion to "identify them as being ... 'Type II Materials'", so ownership of specified work product is not secured.

Minimality fails because the licence rewrite imports fallback-only rights (worldwide/modify/sublicense for business purposes) instead of making the narrower preferred-level fix (a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables, and removal of the "within Customer's Enterprise only" limit).

Suggested fix: keep the Type I default flip and clause e, replace the Type II licence rewrite with deletion of "within Customer's Enterprise only" plus insertion of "perpetual", and add one sentence granting a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any IBM IP embedded in Type I Materials.
Note: new clause e relies on "Content"; confirm it is a defined term in the Base Terms to avoid a dangling reference.
